subject: chemistry_2

verification.note: Unit 5 (Surface Chemistry) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.76-79, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The printed answer, "4% solution of nitro cellulose in a mixture of alcohol and ether is called collodion", is correct and is kept. BOOK GAP (book p.76, VSAQ 7): the book never says what collodion is FOR. It is used to make the semi-permeable membrane of a dialyser and the membrane used in ultrafiltration, which is the only reason it appears in this chapter; that is added here. Nitro cellulose is also written as cellulose nitrate, and both names are given.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Collodion is a 4% solution of nitro
cellulose in a mixture of alcohol and
Nitro cellulose is also called cellulose
steps.why: The definition is a recipe, so the three parts of it are marked: the strength 4%, the solute nitro cellulose, and the solvent, which is a mixture of alcohol and ether and not either one alone.
common_mistakes: Writing alcohol alone or ether alone as the solvent. The solvent is a mixture of the two.
Leaving out the 4%. The strength is part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: 4%, nitro cellulose, alcohol and ether. Three details, one line.
steps.margin_note: All three details carry this mark. Writing only "a solution of nitro cellulose" is incomplete.

steps.label: Where it is used

lines.text: Used to make membranes for dialysis.

lines: The solution is spread as a thin film and
the solvent is allowed to evaporate.
The film left behind is a semi-permeable
Such membranes are used in the dialyser
steps.why: Collodion is in the surface chemistry chapter only because of what the dried film does: ions and small molecules pass through it while colloidal particles do not. That is the property a dialyser needs, so the use is the second half of the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing that the collodion solution is itself the dialysing membrane. The membrane is the dry film left after the alcohol and ether evaporate, not the liquid.
Naming coagulation as the use. Collodion is used for purification by dialysis, not for coagulating a sol.
steps.memory_tip: Dry the film, and it becomes the membrane bag of the dialyser.
steps.margin_note: Name dialysis or ultrafiltration. One named use is enough for this mark.

insider_note: The book prints only the recipe. Add one line on the use, because the question is set in this chapter for the membrane, not for the solution.
